{{Quote|Republics may fall, empires may rise. But the Bounty Hunter Guild stands strong.|From the ''[[Bounty Hunters Guild Handbook]]''|<ref name="The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett">''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]''</ref>}}
The '''Bounty Hunters' Guild''' was an ancient institution that regulated the bounty-hunting trade. It was led by a [[Guild Master/Legends|guildmaster]] who held members to the [[Bounty Hunters' Creed]], the unwritten rules of the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]]. Its rules were the laws that kept bounty hunters together, but the guild was full of loose cannons, who would often break the rules for their own benefit. The guild was more a coalition of the professionals than a proper organization, and rivalries between its houses were a common occurrence. The bounty hunters who joined the guild had the benefit of notifications of bounty postings before they were broadcast through official channels, which gave guild members a head start. Many [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] agents preferred to deal exclusively with guild bounty hunters.

==Organization==
{{Quote|Nobody, not even the Zanibar cannibals of Xo, wants to get on the Guild's bad side.|[[Arack Dostryt|Arack "Deadeye" Dostryt]]|<ref name="The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett"/>}}
The Bounty Hunters' Guild was composed of many smaller guilds that operated nearly independently. Those guilds were loosely held together by the overarching Bounty Hunters' Guild, each with its own organization, regulation, specialties and agendas. The core of the Bounty Hunters' Guild is made up of ten major houses along with a number of smaller groups, each specializing in a unique brand of bounty hunting, but reporting to the guildmaster. Those major Houses were:

*[[Crimson Nova]] (specialized in Jedi)
*[[House Benelex]] (specialized in kidnapping retrieval)
*[[House Neuvalis]] (rarely dealt with outsiders)
*[[House Paramexor]] (specialized in hunting murderers)
*[[House Renliss]] (consisted of female hunters pursuing male bounties)
*[[House Salaktori]]
*[[House Tresario]] (specialized in hunting pirates)
*[[Mantis Syndicate]] (specialized in big groups)
*[[Ragnar Syndicate]] (specializing in unorthodox techniques)
*[[Skine Bounty Hunter College]] (specialists, who were top in a variety of fields)
*[[Slaver Syndicate]] (sometimes turned their bounties over to slavers)

==History==
===Establishment===
[[File:Guild_founders.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Guild Founders [[Thrassk]], [[Teesoo]], [[Saya Ksi]] and [[Keekrim Pon]]]]
With rogue bounty hunters coming into conflict with Jedi Knights more and more often, and leading to an increasing number of [[Death/Legends|deaths]], the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] requested that the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] address the matter. The Senate decided that the best way to regulate the hunters was for the bounty hunters to police themselves. The hunters were allowed to form governing bodies, providing that they adhere to by-laws and create personnel records, leading to the creation of many guilds. Soon, these guilds formed together, creating one overarching group - the Bounty Hunter's Guild. The four founders had a vision of uniting bounty hunters, training apprentices, and encouraging collaboration with the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] and with each other.

One of the Guild's complexes was located on [[Trandosha/Legends|Trandosha]].

===Old Sith Wars===
During the [[Old Sith Wars]], many hunters ceased to follow the Creed, giving in to the dark, desperate mood of the times. With the Jedi nearly extinct, [[G0-T0|Goto]], leader of the [[Exchange]] on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]] put out a bounty in the hope that the guild's members would bring them alive; however, many thought of it as a decree to destroy Jedi and attempted to kill known survivors. Members of the Guild on Nar Shaddaa turned on each other in eagerness to capture [[Meetra Surik]]. [[Vossk]], the leader of the Guild, was one of the few loyal to the Creed.

===Great Peace of the Republicc===
[[File:BountyHuntersCreed-SWI99.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The Bounty Hunters' Creed]]
A few years after [[900 BBY/Legends|900 BBY]], a [[Human/Legends|Human]]-only faction was created, forming a schism in the Guild. They invaded [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] territory, and the Mandalorians [[Ixtlar incident|retaliated]] by exploding the location of their first meeting - a [[Space station/Legends|space station]] at [[Ixtlar/Legends|Ixtlar]] - killing them all. This pushed the Guild to recruit members of many different [[Species/Legends|species]], to prove that the Guild was not [[Speciesism|speciesist]]. Even [[Droid/Legends|droids]] were allowed to join.

In [[200 BBY/Legends|200 BBY]], the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]] won a [[Mandalorian–Ithullan war|war]] against the [[Ithullan]]s and proceeded to exterminate the entire Ithullan species. The [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] failed to take any action against the Mandalorians, so a number of rogue [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] teamed up with the Bounty Hunters' Guild to take down the ruling [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|Mandalore]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref>

Following his departure from the [[Cularin system/Legends|Cularin system]] in [[53 BBY/Legends|53 BBY]], the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Riboga]] placed a [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] on the [[Gran/Legends|Gran]] [[Nadin Paal]], which could only be collected if Paal ever left the Cularin system. The Bounty Hunters' Guild sent some of its minions to the system, to monitor Paal's movements, so that they would know if he ever left.<ref name="LFCG">''[[Living Force Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

The maverick Jedi, [[Jon Antilles]], former apprentice of the Dark Woman, infiltrated the Guild prior to the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], bringing many murderers to justice.

===The Clone Wars===
[[File:JustissSW89.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Crimson Nova was a branch within the guild started by Mika.]]
During the Clone Wars, the [[Crimson Nova]] chapter, under the leadership of [[Mika (Farghul)|Mika]], sanctioned a bounty on Jedi offered by [[Kh'aris Fenn]]. This was in direct contradiction to the history of the Guild's alliance with the Republic. Mika, crazed by her hatred of Jedi, refused to end the bounty when [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]], [[Agen Kolar/Legends|Agen Kolar]], [[Saesee Tiin/Legends|Saesee Tiin]], and [[Kit Fisto/Legends|Kit Fisto]] arrived on her space station. The Jedi captured Mika, and [[Stroth]], former leader of the chapter, took over and agreed to end the bounty and turn over Kh'aris Fenn to the Republic.

===Galactic Civil War===
The Guild itself survived under the leadership of the [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshan]] [[Cradossk/Legends|Cradossk]], father of [[Bossk/Legends|Bossk]], where it acted as a formal allied holding to the Empire. According to the official field manual for the Imperial forces, the ''[[Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]'', the reason for this working relationship was because of the belief among bounty hunters that "the highest bid makes the rules."<ref name="IHB">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref> This continued until around [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]], when it was destroyed through the manipulation of [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]]. The plan itself was the work of [[Prince/Legends|Prince]] [[Xizor/Legends|Xizor]], who enlisted [[Kud'ar Mub'at]] as a middleman between himself and Fett.

[[File:Bounty_Hunters_Guild_propaganda_poster.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A propaganda poster for the Bounty Hunters' Guild. [[Aurebesh]] caption reads "WHEN NO ONE ELSE CAN GET IT DONE," ''[sic]''.]]
Fett, who was known for his disdain of the Guild, joined it, tearing it into two factions: the [[True Guild]] and the [[Guild Reform Committee]]. The True Guild was composed of the elders who had run the Guild and reaped the profits, igniting the resentment of the younger, bounty-earning members who formed the Guild Reform Committee. This manipulation resulted in the [[Bounty Hunter Wars]]. The weak hunters were crushed, leaving only the strong to be hired by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]]. During the conflict, Bossk killed and devoured his father.

In the aftermath of the Bounty Hunter Wars, only [[Dengar/Legends|Dengar]], Bossk, and several others were left alive. Boba Fett and Dengar once teamed up to capture [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] but failed, marking the end of their partnership. Bossk eventually retired. [[Zuckuss/Legends|Zuckuss]] and [[4-LOM/Legends|4-LOM]] split up and hunted fewer and fewer bounties.

Later during the war, the same belief about the highest bid making the rules was ultimately what resulted in the Guild siding with the Rebels.<ref name="IHB" />

===Second Imperial Civil War===
By 137 ABY, the Guild remained active. It had been infiltrated by [[Azlyn Rae]], a former [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] and undercover member of the [[Imperial Knight]]s. [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] assassin [[Ku Vrat]] had been a member of the Guild until he was expelled for interfering with other hunters' bounties.
